crop.notes: Whole reprinted article, headline to end.

title.suggested: Few Champion Pugilists Kept Their Money

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic reprinted a New York Herald piece on how champion pugilists made and lost fortunes. It noted that old Tom Allen, beaten by Jem Mace, was 'living after a fashion in St. Louis.'

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republic: St. Louis, Mo., Friday Morning, December 28, 1888, page 6. Reprinted from the New York Herald.

facts.fact: Allen lost to Jem Mace, said to be not far from the spot where John L. Sullivan beat Paddy Ryan
In late 1888 Allen was described as 'living after a fashion in St. Louis', one of many old champions without much money

notes: Current title 'Jem Mace Defeats Tom Allen' is misleading; the article is a general piece on boxers' finances and mentions Allen in one sentence. Current summary does not mention Allen.
